extracted.intended_audience: publishers and authors submitting works for the Edgar® Awards (Mystery Writers of America)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and submission requirements for entering books, short stories, television/teleplays, and specific named awards in the Mystery Writers of America Edgar® Awards (works published in 2026 for the 2027 awards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category correctness / disqualification
rubrics_metrics.description: MWA will disqualify a work from consideration if it is entered in the wrong category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please read category information for complete information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-committee submission rule
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of the Robert L. Fish, the Sue Grafton Memorial Award, the Mary Higgins Clark and the Lilian Jackson Braun awards, a work may be submitted to only one Edgar® committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is the responsibility of the publisher or producer to submit works to the appropriate committee. MWA will disqualify a work from consideration if it is entered in the wrong category.

rubrics_metrics.name: One copy per judge requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: One copy of each eligible work must be sent to each member of the proper committee along with a copy of the submission form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the MWA National Headquarters for a list of the judges’ names and addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include promotional materials with entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Do NOT include reviews or other promotional materials along with your entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital files must be sent 'clean,' i.e. with no sales/promotion/quotes material attached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not contact judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Do NOT contact the judges regarding this or any other submission (beyond sending the books).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contacting the judges directly might make this submission ineligible for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completed entry form required
rubrics_metrics.description: A completed entry form is required for submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the online submission form and email it to each judge along with the digital file of the book/story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active Status membership eligibility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All works submitted for consideration must meet the requirements for Active Status membership as described in the membership guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the author does not need to be a member of MWA, the work itself must make the author eligible for active status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-published works ineligible
rubrics_metrics.description: At this time, self-published work is not eligible for Edgar Award consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher must be on approved list / vetting required
rubrics_metrics.description: All publishers submitting work must be on MWA’s approved publisher list or otherwise qualify to be added to that list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a publisher not yet on the list qualifies to be added, they must contact the MWA national office to begin the vetting process. All such requests must be approved by the national board before the final submission deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short story minimum payment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Short stories must have paid the author a minimum of $25 to be eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, the author must have received at least $25 from that publisher in advance money or royalties before the story is submitted to MWA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission by publisher preferred
rubrics_metrics.description: Works should be submitted by the publisher, but may also be submitted by the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects the confidentiality of the judging and, for hard copy submissions, saves the author costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: No entry fee and no limit on number of entries
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no entry fee, and no limit to the number of entries from a publisher or an individual author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow judges' requested format for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Almost all of our judges will accept books/stories in digital format. You must send the book/story in the format as requested by the judge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Their email addresses are noted on the Judges’ mailing list; check individual judge preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online submission form + email digital file to each judge
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the online submission form, and email it to each judge along with digital file of the book/story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There can be NO expiration date associated with the files. Just as you would be giving them the hardcover or paperback, you are giving them the e-book without any restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital files must have no expiration date
rubrics_metrics.description: There can be NO expiration date associated with the files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files should be delivered as the judge would receive a hardcover/paperback — without restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: File naming requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Please make sure the file name is the book title, not a string of numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not direct judges to retailer or ARC platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: You may NOT send the judge to either Amazon, iBooks, NetGalley or Edelweiss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All digital files MUST be sent to judges directly and 'clean' with no promotional material attached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital files must be 'clean' (no sales/promotion/quotes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital files MUST be sent to judges 'clean,' i.e. with no sales/promotion/quotes material attached.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A few judges will accept PDF files -– check with the national office or committee chair before you send them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pdf may not have any watermarks, be password protected or fixed at a tiny font -– it needs to be readable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final book only; no advance reading copies generally
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the 'final' book may be submitted – no advance reading copies or galleys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Galleys/ARCs – absolutely NO watermarks on the pages -– it makes it almost impossible to read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited allowance for galleys/ARCs (Nov/Dec releases)
rubrics_metrics.description: PLEASE NOTE: Only works with a November or December release date may be submitted to judges in galley/ARC form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All works MUST ARRIVE by the judges by December 7, 2026. Works received after that date will not be considered for an Edgar award. Absolutely no exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short story anthology/magazine submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For short stories, if you are submitting an anthology/magazine, you must email the table of contents to the national office and mark if there are stories that are either not eligible or are eligible for the Robert Fish award.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-authenticity acknowledgment required on forms
rubrics_metrics.description: All forms must have the following acknowledged: a declaration that substantive content is free of AI-generated material, and that AI assistive tools, if used, were limited to assistive roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact required text: 'To ensure originality and authenticity, we require all writers and publishers submitting work to verify that the substantive content of their submission is free of AI-generated material. While AI assistive tools may be used in supportive roles—such as for copy editing, grammar checking, or formatting improvements—core elements of the submission, including narrative, thematic development, and stylistic choices, should reflect the author’s unique voice and creative work. By submitting, you confirm that AI tools have only been used in a limited, assistive capacity and that the work remains an authentic representation of the author’s creative intent and voice.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Author follow-up if publisher does not submit
rubrics_metrics.description: If the publisher has not submitted a work within 60 days of the publication date, the author should notify the MWA national office, who will contact the publisher to get the work submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the national office cannot get the publisher to submit in a timely fashion, they will notify the author of how to submit the book/story directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing and arrival-to-judges deadline (within 30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: The book MUST arrive to the judges within 30 days of sending the submission form to the national office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please do NOT fill out the submission form until the book is ready to be sent to the judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested schedule for submissions by publication month
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested submission schedule to assist the judging committee (not a requirement for eligibility): lists specific 'submit by' dates for works published each month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Works published January–March 2026 submit by April 30, 2026; October–December 31, 2026 submit by December 7, 2026. Meeting these deadlines greatly aids the judging process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute final deadline for judge receipt (no exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: All works MUST ARRIVE by the judges by December 7, 2026. Works received after that date will not be considered for an Edgar award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolutely no exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominations and awards timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations are usually announced in the middle of January of the following year and winners are announced at the annual Edgar® Awards Banquet in late April or early May.
